newsitem.title: UK: Wet Brent crude market murky, sour, W.African ease.
newsitem.headline: Wet Brent crude market murky, sour, W.African ease.

text.p: A lack of activity on the North Sea physical crude markets on Friday morning meant that confusion over the value of Dated Brent persisted.
"It's hard to get a handle on this market..It's being pushed in both directions," said one trader.
Aggressive selling by a Wall Street trader helped to weaken the Brent paper curve.
A CFD for March 3-7 was traded at April Brent +17 cents, equivalent to around March Brent -20 cents, signalling a fall off in wet Brent from recent traded levels.
But another trading house, which has fixed a ULCC to take Brent to South Africa in March, was bidding on the wet market as high as April Brent +30 cents for Brent loading March 3-9.
"There's a battle evolving here," a trader said.
CFDs for next week (Feb 24-28) traded at April Brent +26 cents, while March 10-14 traded twice at April +6 cents.
March/April softened from trades of +40 and +42 cents in the U.S. aftermarket to talk at +36/40. April/May sold twice at +25.
Outright Brent values fell, with April Brent trading 22 cents down at $19.86 a barrel at 1320 GMT on the IPE, the first time the spot contract has slipped below $20 since last August.

Three cargoes from the original March Brent loading programme were to be nominated from the paper chains on Friday. Traders said that top-up barrels in the March 8-10 window might also be put together to make another cargo.

In the Mediterranean, traders saw continuing offers of spot volumes of Iraq's Kirkuk, including one taken by Mineralimpex last week, and assessed the grade at around 30 cents below March's official Kirkuk selling price of Dated Brent -$1.55.
Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organisation (SOMO) is touting extra spot volumes to make up for a shortfall in revenue from the U.N. oil-for food plan caused by falling world oil prices.
